answer: Relic thinking won't stop sybils; economic terrain does. Treat each meadow of accounts as a mesa with one narrow path: registration requires a sponsor from an existing web-of-trust, and sponsors stake reputation that gets slashed if their referred identity is later convicted. Attackers must therefore buy whole chains of honest history, not mint fresh keys — every forged identity inherits a traceable lineage, and burning the sponsor's stake makes renting bot armies more expensive than any one-epoch payout.
